theme: The priest-king who ascended on high
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 110. You have read this psalm before, with Peter’s sermons and Acts. Read it now with Ephesians in mind: it is the psalm of the ascended king, seated at God’s right hand, who is also a priest forever.
settingTheScene: Psalm 110 is the Old Testament verse most quoted in the New Testament. Jesus used it to stump the Pharisees (Matthew 22:41-46). Peter used it at Pentecost (Acts 2:34-35). The writer of Hebrews builds an entire argument on verse 4. In Ephesians 1:20-22, Paul draws on verse 1 when he says God seated Christ at his right hand, far above all rule and authority. Paired with Psalm 68, which describes the ascent, this psalm shows the seat and office of the ascended Christ.
observation: “The LORD says to my Lord: Sit at my right hand” (v. 1).
“Until I make your enemies your footstool” (v. 1).
“The LORD sends forth from Zion your mighty scepter” (v. 2).
“Your people will offer themselves freely on the day of your power” (v. 3).
“The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind” (v. 4).
“You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek” (v. 4).
“He will shatter kings on the day of his wrath” (v. 5).
“Therefore he will lift up his head” (v. 7).
interpretation:
The psalm is a conversation within God. “The LORD says to my Lord.” David speaks of two: the LORD (Yahweh) and “my Lord” (Adonai), someone David himself calls Lord. Jesus pointed this out: “If David thus calls him Lord, how is he his son?” The answer is that the Messiah is both David’s descendant and David’s Lord, human and divine. The invitation: “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.” To sit at the right hand is to share the throne. Paul says this is where Christ now is (Ephesians 1:20; Colossians 3:1).

Verse 2 says the king rules from Zion in the midst of his enemies. His reign is real now, though not yet fully visible. Verse 3 describes his people: “Your people will offer themselves freely on the day of your power.” The king’s people are volunteers, willing servants. “In holy garments” (or splendor of holiness), they come like the dew of the morning. They are a new generation, drawn by the king’s power, not forced.

Verse 4 is the astonishing center: “The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind, You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.” In Israel, kings came from Judah and priests from Levi. But here the king is also a priest, not of the Levitical order but of Melchizedek, the mysterious priest-king of Salem who blessed Abraham (Genesis 14:18-20). The writer of Hebrews explains that Christ is a high priest of a better order, with an oath, who lives forever and therefore has a permanent priesthood. Because he is a priest-king, he can intercede for us and rule us.

Verses 5 to 7 return to the king’s victories. The Lord at your right hand “will shatter kings on the day of his wrath. He will execute judgment among the nations.” This is the final judgment. The psalm ends, “He will drink from the brook by the way; therefore he will lift up his head.” The victorious king pauses to drink and goes on; his head is lifted in triumph. For Christians, the picture ties together the cross (the brook by the way, the suffering) and the exaltation.

Reading this psalm with Ephesians, we see that Christ’s ascension was not an absence but an enthronement. He now rules, intercedes, and gives gifts. We live between his ascension and his return, with confidence that he reigns.
connection: Genesis 14:17-20 introduces Melchizedek. Matthew 22:41-46, Acts 2:29-36, and Hebrews 1:13, 5:6, 7:1-28 quote or use the psalm. Ephesians 1:20-23 and Colossians 3:1 speak of being seated at God’s right hand. 1 Corinthians 15:25 says he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. Zechariah 6:12-13 speaks of a priest on the throne. Revelation 19:11-16 shows the victorious king. Romans 8:34 says Christ is at the right hand of God, interceding for us. Psalm 2 is a companion royal psalm.
application:
Remember when anxious that Christ is seated at God’s right hand, ruling all things.

Give thanks that your high priest lives forever to intercede for you.

Offer yourself freely to him today, as one of the willing people of verse 3.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for sitting at the Father’s right hand.
Thank him that he is a priest forever.
Ask him to make his enemies his footstool in your life.
